strings.name: Zanele Muholi
strings.summary: Muholi uses portraits, self-portraits and community archives to document Black LGBTQIA+ lives in South Africa, treating those photographed as participants with agency and dignity. Faces and Phases follows people through life changes; Somnyama Ngonyama uses self-representation to question labor and racialized looking. They also build media and arts-education platforms and received the 2026 Hasselblad Award.

strings.highlights.h1.title: An ongoing community portrait
strings.highlights.h1.text: Faces and Phases returns to participants across their lives, combining portraits and personal testimony.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Self-portraits and public expression
strings.highlights.h2.text: Somnyama Ngonyama turns the body, everyday objects and historical memory into questions of representation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Received the 2026 Hasselblad Award
strings.timeline.t1.text: Accepted in Gothenburg and led the accompanying exhibition tour the next day, emphasizing community recognition.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Major Tate exhibition returned
strings.timeline.t2.text: The London show expanded the earlier survey with photography and new sculptural work.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Founded the Muholi Art Institute
strings.timeline.t3.text: Created a platform supporting emerging artists across disciplines.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Began Somnyama Ngonyama
strings.timeline.t4.text: The self-portrait series used costume, ordinary objects and heightened contrast to challenge historical images of Black bodies.
strings.timeline.t5.title: MFA and Inkanyiso established
strings.timeline.t5.text: Completed documentary media study and founded a media platform for queer visual activism.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Launched Faces and Phases
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began a portrait archive of Black queer communities, continuing to follow people through different life stages.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Held a first solo exhibition
strings.timeline.t7.text: Showed Only Half the Picture at Johannesburg Art Gallery, addressing intimacy and experiences of violence.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed advanced photography training
strings.timeline.t8.text: Studied at the Market Photo Workshop, connecting photography and community expression.
